To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the striatum is involved in learning and memory and that α-synucleopathies may impair these functions by affecting synaptic mechanisms that are critical for the storage of memory traces.

1) the interaction between basal ganglia, limbic and cortical areas, is essential for learning and memory processes and 2) the synaptic mechanisms underlying cognitive function are altered in experimental models of Parkinson’s disease.

the α-synucleins accumulation in the basal ganglia and hippocampus is associated with alterations in synaptic plasticity and memory function, and that the striatal and hippocampi α-synucleinis pathology are associated with the same molecular mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms underlying the interaction between the basal ganglia and hippocampal memory systems in physiological and pathological conditions.
the study of molecular, cellular and behavioral mechanisms of memory processes in the hippocampus and basal ganglia, and the role of these brain areas in cognitive functions.
the molecular mechanisms of LTP in the basal ganglia and the hippocampus, and with the functional consequences of LTP on the memory processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the basal ganglia and the hippocampal/ limbic system, in the context of a complex and dynamic interaction, play a critical role in the acquisition of memory and in the modulation of the cognitive functions.

the basal ganglia are not only involved in motor control, but also play a role in the control of cognitive functions, and the hippocampus is not only engaged in declarative memory processes, but is also involved in non-declarative learning.

α-synucleins may play an important role as a key component of the molecular machinery underlying the synaptic plasticity of basal ganglia and hippocampus, two structures critically involved in memory processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

α-synucleins may play a role in the pathogenesis of cognitive deficits in Parkinson's disease by altering the synaptic plasticity in the striatum and hippocampus, and that this alteration may be mediated by the modulation of the dopaminergic and cholinergic neurotransmitter systems.
in Parkinson's disease, the striatum and hippocampus are affected by a common molecular mechanism, i.e., abnormal accumulation of α-Synuclein.
the striatum and hippocampus are two distinct memory systems that are able to work together in a dynamic way to integrate and adjust behavioral responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the striatum and hippocampus are not independent systems but rather interact with each other to form a complex memory network.
the α-synucleins' role as an important component of the molecular machinery involved in the formation of long-lasting synaptic modifications is a common denominator for the two memory systems.

α-synucleins are involved in memory processes and in their alteration, and that the mechanisms by which α-synucleines are involved in memory impairment are likely to be different in the striatum and in the hippocampus.
